newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinian first sentenced to death gets life.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian first sentenced to death gets life.

text.p: An Israeli military court on Sunday handed down a new sentence to a Palestinian originally given the death sentence for plotting a suicide bus bombing that killed six people in Israel, the army said.
It said Said Badarneh, 27, was sentenced to life in prison plus 30 years after being convicted, in a retrial, of involvement in the bombing.
In June 1995, a military appeals court overturned the death sentence given Badarneh in his first trial.
It ordered a retrial, saying the lower court made mistakes before it found Badarneh guilty in November 1994 for sending a suicide bomber to blow up the bus in April of that year.
The bombing in Hadera, north of Tel Aviv, killed five Israelis and the bomber and wounded 30 people.
Israel has only once carried out the death sentence, in 1962 against Adolf Eichmann, a mastermind of the Nazi German Holocaust during World War Two.
It has refrained from ordering the death penalty for fear of Palestinian reprisals and all previous military death sentences were reversed.
